genZNote: By age 2, almost everyone has already had this one — it's the classic cause of roseola: days of high fever, then a rash right as the fever breaks.

morphology.shape: Enveloped icosahedral virion with tegument layer

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human salivary glands and T lymphocytes
habitat.hostAssociation: Humans are the sole host; establishes lifelong latency after primary infection, typically in early childhood
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans; shed in saliva even from asymptomatic adults, driving near-universal childhood exposure

culture.growthCharacteristics: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; PCR or serology used when confirmation is needed

identificationClues: Classic presentation is roseola infantum (exanthem subitum, 'sixth disease'): several days of high fever in an otherwise well-appearing infant, followed by an abrupt rose-pink rash as the fever resolves
Nearly universal infection by age 2, usually via asymptomatic viral shedding in saliva from caregivers
Like other herpesviruses, establishes lifelong latency (in monocytes/T cells) after primary infection and can reactivate in immunocompromised hosts
A classically taught cause of febrile seizures in young children due to the abrupt high fevers it produces

diseases: Reactivation disease in immunocompromised/transplant patients (encephalitis, marrow suppression)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Saliva contact, typically from asymptomatically shedding caregivers/family members
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common viral infections of early childhood, with near-universal seroprevalence by age 2-3
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Usually a clinical diagnosis; PCR/serology reserved for atypical presentations or immunocompromised patients

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — usually a clinical diagnosis
examFacts.importantDisease: Roseola infantum (high fever followed by rash on defervescence)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Nearly universal childhood herpesvirus infection; classic 'fever then rash' pattern distinguishes it from most other childhood exanthems (rash appears with fever)
